summary: This Wikipedia article describes drifting, a driving technique in which the driver intentionally oversteers with loss of traction while keeping control through a corner. It covers the technique's history from pre-1950 Europe to 1970s Japan, the competition format and judging criteria in series such as D1 Grand Prix and Formula Drift, and the car setup, tuning and tire choices involved. It also covers R/C drifting and drifting's presence in film, television and video games. The note is truncated before its final sections.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of drifting, the motorsport technique of oversteering through corners, covering its history, judged competition, drift car tuning, and media depictions.
key_facts: Drifting is a driving technique where the driver intentionally oversteers, with loss of traction, while maintaining control through the entirety of a corner or turn.
Drifting is traditionally performed using three methods: clutch kicking, weight transfer (such as the Scandinavian flick), and employing a handbrake turn.
Enzo Ferrari credits Italian driver Tazio Nuvolari as the inventor of the four-wheel drift.
Keiichi Tsuchiya, known as the 'Drift King', helped organize one of the first events specifically for drifting, the Ikaten, in 1988.
One of the earliest recorded drift events outside Japan took place in 1996 at Willow Springs Raceway in Willow Springs, California, hosted by Option magazine.
Judges score drifters on Speed/Fluidity, Angle, Line and Style.
In the final stage, drivers compete in tandem passes called 'chases' (tsuiso), and the best of the eight heats advance to the next four, then the next two, then the final.
Overtaking the lead car under grip conditions automatically forfeits a pass.
A mechanical limited slip differential (LSD) is considered essential for drifting, and the preferred form is the clutch type in two-way form.
Formula Drift is described as the top United States drifting series, and its style is judged on initiation, fluidity and commitment.
In the 2005 D1GP top 10, the Nissan Silvia S15 appeared three times and the Toyota Levin/Trueno AE86 appeared twice.
The 2019 Netflix television series Hyperdrive is a reality competition show focused heavily on drifting, won by Diego Higa of Brazil.
Baby Driver (2017) features an extended drifting chase scene in which Ansel Elgort's character drives a Subaru WRX.
Initial D is a 1995 manga series that helped spread drifting internationally and follows Takumi Fujiwara, who learns to drift in a custom Toyota AE86.
